tagline: From farms and vineyards toward a reservoir that submerged a town
intro: Interlake Road leaves Jolon Road just south of Lockwood and runs toward Lake San Antonio. At the Lockwood end, farms, cattle ranches and vineyards occupy a broad valley enclosed by coastal mountains. Caltrans recognizes the section from Jolon Road to the San Luis Obispo County line as an officially designated County Scenic Highway.

That designation dates to 1971; the adjoining Interlake Road–Nacimiento Drive segment received its own designation in 1972. The lake had already changed the valley: San Antonio Dam was completed in 1965, and the reservoir submerged the town of Pleyto. The reservoir’s main purpose is groundwater supply, keeping water in the river through the year so it can seep into the ground.

Begin at the Jolon Road junction south of Lockwood, where Interlake Road carries the G14 county-route number. Follow it south toward Lake San Antonio and the county line. Beyond this segment, the separately designated scenic road continues to Chimney Rock Road in San Luis Obispo County.

moments.title: Lockwood
moments.text: Lockwood’s name honors Belva Lockwood, the Equal Rights Party’s presidential candidate in 1884 and 1888. The community’s first post office opened in 1888, the year of her second campaign. The setting is a broad valley surrounded by coastal mountains, with farms, ranches and vineyards. San Antonio Valley Vineyards are part of the community, along with olive groves and extensive land for cattle grazing. A post office and community center serve Lockwood. The town lies nine miles northwest of Lake San Antonio and six miles east-southeast of Jolon, in southern Monterey County.

moments.title: Rancho Pleyto
moments.text: Much of Rancho Pleyto is beneath Lake San Antonio, including the later town of Pleyto. Governor Pío Pico granted the land to Antonio Chaves in 1845; it extended along the San Antonio River southeast of Jolon. After California passed to the United States, a claim for the grant was filed with the Public Land Commission in 1852. William Pinkerton bought a large portion in 1868 and founded Pleyto. The grant was patented to William S. Johnson and Preston K. Woodside in 1872. The creation of Lake San Antonio completely submerged the town.

moments.title: Lake San Antonio
moments.text: The reservoir lies primarily in southern Monterey County, with part extending into northern San Luis Obispo County. Lake San Antonio’s principal job is to replenish groundwater. Stored water keeps the San Antonio River flowing through the year, allowing more of it to seep into the ground. Without the reservoir, the river would be nearly dry during summer. The 202-foot dam was completed in 1965 under Monterey County District Engineer Loran Bunte Jr. Falling water levels in 2014 forced the Wildflower Triathlon to move its swimming leg two miles. Competitors then ran across the former lake bed to reach their bicycles.
